To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of morphological families is a good approach for dealing with derivational variation, but that it is not enough to deal with the whole problem of word variation; the use of syntactic dependency relations improves significantly the results obtained with the morphological families approach, but the best approach is the mixed one, which combines both morphological families and syntactic dependency relations.

(a) morphological families are a good way to cope with derivational variation, and (b) mixed approaches that combine morphological families with syntactic information are a better way to deal with the content of the documents.

(1) morphological families are a useful resource for the Spanish language; (2) syntactic information is useful for dealing with derivational and semantic variation; and (3) mixed approaches based on the use of both morphological families and syntactic information are more successful than approaches based only on one of them.
In summary, our research is concerned with
finding the most suitable combination of the above techniques for the Spanish Monolingual track.
the development of a new method for term conflation that is based on a mixed approach.
the study of the impact that the application of these techniques has on the performance of a monolingual search system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best approach was the one that combined the use of morphological families with the syntactic dependencies.
the use of a morphological lexicon and a morphological analyser is a necessary step for the development of any information retrieval system.
we have achieved a good level of precision and recall for the single word queries, while the multi-word queries have not given us the desired results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we obtained the best results when we applied the mixed approach, and the worst results when we applied a pure morphological approach.
we obtained the best results in all the cases in which the query was expanded with a fixed similarity threshold.
, in general, the use of morphological information is better than the use of syntactic information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best results are obtained when we apply all the techniques together.
, in general, morphological and syntactic approaches are complementary and can improve the performance in the retrieval process.
, even though we achieved good results in the first three experiments, the mixed approach based on syntactic information was the one which achieved the best performance.
